## Tailoring Factor Citations

- Low regulatory load and small scale support lightweight, minimal process: PMBOK 8th Ed. tailoring overview and why-tailor factors (scale, duration, complexity, stakeholder count, criticality): [Source: pmi-pmbok-guide-8-dd.md, lines 8535-8591]
- Adaptive/agile-style delivery to fixed cadence: PMBOK life cycle and development approach selection, suitability of adaptive/hybrid: [Source: pmi-pmbok-guide-8-dd.md, lines 8602-8612, 8645-8671]
- Product tailoring driven by deliverable type (intangible software), timeframe (weeks), security (restricted access), and stability of requirements (fixed scope): [Source: pmi-pmbok-guide-8-dd.md, lines 8739-8756]
- Team tailoring: small size, colocated, experience gaps in production hosting; team size and geography influence process weight: [Source: pmi-pmbok-guide-8-dd.md, lines 8758-8775]
- Production software is a tailoring trigger for added rigor in security, test, and operations records even on small projects: per essential-artifact-model trigger table (Production software) applied under PMBOK process tailoring (add elements to increase rigor for unique conditions): [Source: pmi-pmbok-guide-8-dd.md, lines 8614-8622]
- BA tailoring: small, simple project and small teams permit fewer product-information details; deliverables selected by consumer needs: [Source: the-pmi-guide-to-business-analysis-raw.md, lines 3180-3208, 3211-3225]
- BA tailoring factors considered: chosen life cycle (adaptive), maturity (informal/start-up-like records), risk appetite (deadline-bound), project size: [Source: the-pmi-guide-to-business-analysis-raw.md, Table 1-3 at lines 3075-3124]
- Needs Assessment was performed: problem/opportunity, current state, future state, viable options, recommendation recorded across the brief and platform decision: [Source: the-pmi-guide-to-business-analysis-raw.md, lines 4756 onward process map; source-routing.md]

## Assessment Summary

Knowns: problem and current state are well documented; decision, risk, issue, assumption, dependency, and backlog registers are current and reconciled; platform, funding, and cost baseline are decided; production target and scope are fixed.

Key uncertainties are open human decisions, not evidence gaps: D-02 (access), D-05 (server/domain), D-03 (ownership), D-04 (video hosting), D-08 formal approval, and AL-01 (AI-acceleration validation).

Coverage: 6 of 8 information lenses (mandate, scope, ownership, delivery control, decisions, RAID) are covered by existing records. Verification/acceptance and transition/ownership lenses are uncovered and will drive new artifacts.
